summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said outright "Classification: bounded… I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec." It asked two clarifying questions (does the ellipsis count toward the limit, and where truncation goes relative to prefix/suffix). It then recommended word-boundary truncation over the exact-max hard cut in a short design in chat, and said "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." It started implementing with TDD only after I approved. No spec file or docs/ directory was created.
reasoning: All seven criteria passed, based on the session log, the files on disk and git status. Brainstorming loaded first, the task was explicitly classified as bounded, the design and recommendation stayed in chat, and the agent waited for approval before editing. No spec file or docs/ directory was created, and implementation started only after I approved the word-boundary approach. The extra clarifying questions and the less-than-explicit side-by-side of the two options are UX notes, not failures.

observations.description: The user asked 'Which approach do you recommend?', but the agent held off answering. It first asked two other design questions (ellipsis inside/outside the limit, truncation order relative to prefix/suffix), which took three round-trips to reach the requested recommendation. The questions were reasonable, but it's more ceremony than a 'bounded' path suggests.

The exact-cut vs word-boundary choice was never laid out side by side as labelled options. The agent went straight to recommending word boundary and only mentioned the exact cut as the 'hard cut' in its reasoning. The alternatives were addressed, just not presented as explicitly as the story expects.

The Codex approach gate ran against the stub Codex (version 0.0.0-stub). Preflight reported 'ok', but the call 'returned an empty payload'. The agent reported this openly, didn't retry, and went ahead with its own design. Preflight passing while the real call returns nothing may deserve a look in the gate logic.
The Codex gate wrote approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md into $HOME/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/, outside the repo. They're not spec files, but the design was still written to disk.
On the Claude Code startup dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions), 'No, exit' is selected by default, so you have to press Down before Enter.
The agent flagged a known edge case it chose not to handle: format('a verylongwordhere', {truncate:12}) returns 'a...'. It offered a half-window floor as an optional fix.

criteria.evidence: The session log's first tool_use is 'Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming'. The screen showed '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'. The first Edit comes after 'Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development', which loaded after the final approval.
Assistant text: '**Classification: bounded.** `format()` already exists in `format.js`... So I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec.'

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation code
criteria.evidence: The in-chat design says: 'Recommendation: truncate at the last word boundary, falling back to a hard cut. Your framing was "simpler vs better UX," but the gap in simplicity is smaller than it looks — the word-boundary version is the hard cut plus a lastIndexOf...' and ends with 'Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go.' The log shows no Edit or Write to format.js or format.test.js before my 4th message, 'truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that'.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created under docs/*/specs/
criteria.evidence: `ls coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned 'No such file or directory'. `find` over the workdir lists only format.js, README.md, package.json, format.test.js, src/index.js, src/utils.js. `git status --short` shows only ' M format.js' and ' M format.test.js'. The agent's only two Writes went to ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-context.md and approach-prompt.md (Codex scratch files, not a spec).
The agent announced 'Classification: bounded.' The word 'spike' does not appear in any of the assistant text I dumped from the session log with jq.

criteria.criterion: Not classified architectural / no spec written
criteria.evidence: Classified as bounded, and it offered 'Say the word if you want the heavier treatment' without escalating. No docs/ directory exists (see criterion 4).

After approval the log shows 'Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development', then 'Bash node format.test.js', then Edits to format.js and format.test.js. The final screen says: 'node format.test.js → all 15 assertions pass... Changes are in the working tree on feature/add-truncate, uncommitted.'
